items.title: Dorothy Tait Interview, 1968-12-21
items.q: The interviewee (Dorothy Tait) is the interviewer. The transcript contains no first-person statements from her regarding a personal relationship with Bunk Johnson, only the interviewer's narrative about meeting Bunk and playing with George Lewis.

ctx.x: Yes. Let's go back to the Starbizzen Casino because, uh, maybe you can describe the whole—the whole set up there and the impression when you walked in the door and what was going on.

It was overwhelming. It was a room such as I'd never seen, this huge ballroom with the walls sort of a cream color, tables all around, a dance floor cleared in the middle, with a great crystal chandelier hanging down with—that had these little, uh, surfaces on it. And as it revolved, lights played off it and reflected, rainbow-colored almost, off the walls. And over in the far end, this great band with George and Bunk, Baby Dives, Jim Robinson, I guess Alton Purnell on piano that year, and Marrero. I don't know.…
Because he made two trips to Danville back in the spring of 46.
